result.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics-Aware Industrial Anomaly Detection and Reasoning
result.comment: Accepted at IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV) 2027
result.summary: Industrial Anomaly Detection (IAD) is a long-established problem that aims to detect defects in industrial products during manufacturing for quality control. Most existing studies focus on static visual patterns as the basis for detection. However, in real manufacturing environments, many anomalies are dynamics-based, such as irregular movements that cannot be perceived from static cues alone. We observe that even recent Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM)-based approaches fall short in identifying such dynamic anomalies due to limited temporal modeling capability. To address this, we introduce MUSTARD: MUltimodal SpatioTemporal Anomaly Reasoning and Detection, a framework that equips MLLMs with fine-grained spatiotemporal dynamics awareness for detecting and reasoning about dynamics-based defects. MUSTARD introduces optical-flow-guided keyframe selection and augmented modalities to capture critical motion irregularities through local motion patterns and global dynamic evolution. Its normal pattern-based reasoning pipeline requires only a few normal reference samples as the detection basis, avoiding any model updates. This enables efficient adaptation across various products and provides high decision interpretability. MUSTARD is the first MLLM-based framework for dynamics-based IAD. Experiments demonstrate its superior performance in detecting spatiotemporal anomalies and providing plausible explanations. The code will be made publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文面向工业异常检测中依赖运动而非静态外观的缺陷，提出 MUSTARD 框架，通过光流引导的关键帧选择与增强模态为 MLLM 补充细粒度时空动态信息，并以少量正常参考样本做对比式推理，无需模型更新。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按运动显著性挑帧并送入 MLLM」的做法可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与有限 token 下细节保留提供可供核查的线索，但论文不涉及 latent 推理状态或答案使用内部表示的机制，联系主要在输入侧证据构造。
